Subject: [unmarked] Modelling variation in abundance - multi year data set

Hi all,

I just went through the paper on modelling variation in abundance using unmarked and have two questions.  Am I correct in assuming that one could also analyse a multi-year data set using unmarked (similar to the robust design)? In addition, is it possible to improve abundance estimates precision of the individual surveys by maximizing the content information if data from more than one survey is available? I tried analysing my individual data sets (n =6) in SPACECAP, but simulations converged poorly.

Thanks

Ezequiel

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Modelling variation in abundance - multi year data set
parts:
hi Ezequiel,
 SPACECAP fits individual encounter history models and unless you have a lot of recaptures you probably can't expect much with n = 6 observations.

 unmarked can fit multi-year models using either the pcount() function, where you could model year as a polynomial trend or in relation to fixed covariates, or you can use pcountOpen which fits a fully dynamic model.
An example of the former is here:
@article{kery2009trend, title={Trend estimation in populations with imperfect detection}, author={Kery, M. and Dorazio, R.M. and Soldaat, L. and Van Strien, A. and Zuiderwijk, A. and Royle, J.A.}, journal={Journal of Applied Ecology}, volume={46}, number={6}, pages={1163--1172}, year={2009}, publisher={Wiley Online Library} }

regards
andy
